summary: ReelLab Studio v6 launch verification — backend 15/15 pytest pass; frontend DOM checks for nav (studio_owner vs CEO), invoices CEO gating, MOCKED text removal, Content Studio testids, and CEO Access Control all pass. Register form correctly enforces separate first/last name fields and blocks API call on empty last_name. Caption AI returns 3 captions via Claude. Coupons accept promotional + group_tag and round-trip via GET.
action_items: (Optional) Confirm the inline error string for empty last_name on /register — the client correctly blocks the API call (URL stayed on /register) but the literal text 'Last name is required.' was not found in DOM under common error selectors. Functionally fine; verify copy if exact wording matters.

(Optional/test-doc) Note that in the standalone caption-gen modal, platform testids are 'gen-platform-<key>' (e.g. gen-platform-instagram). The 'platform-<key>' testids live on the per-day post-modal. Spec mentions both; both exist — just under different parent components.
critical_code_review_comments: ContentStudio post endpoints require the full ContentPostIn body on PATCH (title/platform/scheduled_for/caption). If you want true partial PATCH behavior, change the handler to accept Optional[...] fields or split into a separate UpdateIn schema. Current behaviour is acceptable but the verb is misleading — consider PUT or making it partial.

/api/content/posts response shapes are mixed: POST returns {post:{...}}, GET returns {posts:[...]}, PATCH/DELETE return {ok:true}. Frontend works, but a unified envelope (always {post}/{posts}) would simplify clients and tests.
Register flow: server returns user with first_name/last_name and display_name = first+' '+last — looks good. Consider trimming whitespace before composing display_name.

CEO Access Control: ac-group-tag only renders when promotional=true. Test scripts must toggle ac-promotional ON before asserting the field. Consider rendering the input disabled-but-visible so testability is unconditional.
/api/auth/me wraps response as {user:{...}, ...} — consistent with login. Confirmed via tests.
